native_review.summary: The conversation successfully resolved the user's request. The agent authenticated Daiki Sanchez (email lookup failed due to a database mismatch, then name+zip succeeded), correctly declined splitting payment across two cards, informed the user that the most expensive item was the Action Camera at $481.50, correctly stated that individual items cannot be cancelled, and then helped switch all items to their cheapest available options, bringing the total down to $1130.85 with a $36.13 refund to the user's Visa. The user confirmed the modification, and the order was updated successfully. The only issues were procedural: the agent violated the one-tool-call-at-a-time policy by making five parallel get_product_details calls in turn 18, and responded to the user while making a tool call in turn 12. These were minor and did not affect the outcome. The natural language assertions (most expensive item is the camera; camera costs $481.50) were satisfied.

The policy states that if the agent takes a tool call, it should not respond to the user at the same time. This is a minor procedural violation that did not affect the outcome.
